axis: flat publication of what was hidden → a confidence spilled to the teller's discredit

members.tone: Puts the hidden thing into public circulation all at once, with the abruptness of the arrival rather than any blame as its whole character.
Here the act is the telling, not the finding: flat about how the thing got out and saying only that it is now public.
The neutral centre the others specialise — something hidden is made visible, with no comment on who loses by it.
Strips the cover off with the implication that the thing was kept back for a reason, so the telling lands as a charge against whoever kept it.
Formal and procedural: it makes the matter public without the flavour of trust broken that *divulge* carries.
Keeps the secrecy in view — what is told was meant to be kept, so the telling registers as a breach.
Treats the matter as buried rather than merely untold, so the digging is part of the word in a way it is not in *reveal*.
The bare verb for someone entrusted failing to stay quiet; it names no content, only that the confidence got out of them.
The revealing wrecks what it reveals — where *disclose* only makes a thing known, this one endangers it in the same motion.
Contemptuous: the secret is handed over the way an informer hands it over, and the handing over is the disgrace.
All timing and no secrecy — whether the thing is produced or disclosed, the force of the word is that it arrives with no warning.
The teller never meant to tell: the thing escapes and gives the person away, so the fault is in the letting slip rather than the intent.
What the word specifies is the missing name — the telling happens with the teller kept out of sight, and it passes no verdict on what is told.
The one telling here that keeps the secret a secret: it goes to a single hearer in trust, where *divulge* gives it away.
Dismissive — the confidence falls out of an ungoverned mouth for no motive beyond the pleasure of talking.
